questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I am very fond of the mountains both in regards to skiing and hiking and therefore thought it would be ideal to go to Switzerland to be able to spend my free time in the mountains. 
I also wanted to go to a German speaking country to improve my German. 
I heard that UZH is a very good Uni with a high academic level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
There is always a lot of information upon arrival. Everything always work out, so dont stress too much. 
I received a very adequate information sheet from UZH about everything I needed to know before and upon arrival which was very helpfull. Furthermore I got the needed information from the student housing before my arrival also. So you are provided with the information you need by email! Not much need to search for it yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I attended a welcome event where you receive information about registering in the country, helath insurance exemption and the SEMP scholarship (if granted one). 
There is an student service office in the main building where it was easy to get your questions answeared. Otherwise they student service was very quick at replying to emails!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You receive an email in which you are asked whether you would like to be offered housing through the univeristy. I accepted this offer, and later received an offer for a room at a dorm which I accepted.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You cannot live on UZH. However you can live on one of the ETH campus' but most students live off campus. So no worries! There are a lot of social events happening at campus and off campus in which you can easily participate, if you wish.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registering for the courses was very easy! Also you can register/deregister until some time in October, which gives you the opportunity to try out different courses before you finally decide which ones you will be taking.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Maybe a guide at UZH website. But it was very easy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I even registered for some courses I didnt want to take at the end, and also then was it very easy to deregister.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just go to studenter service website, search the course you want and register. Very easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is high! So you do need to study a lot of you go to UZH. But very interesting courses!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I took only economics courses. Like at UCPH there were lectures and exercise classes in each course. The lectures were very similar to what I was used to but in the exercise classes I was used to from UCPH to do the given assignments myself with help from at TA. At UZH it was however the TA who went over all the exercises and you were just taking notes. 
Also all the exams are handwritten.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Behavioral Finance
Labor Economics
Public Debt Management
Global Poverty & Development Economics
Advanced Microeconomics I
Advanced Macroeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you are and BA economics students take
Advanced Microeconomics I
Advanced Macroeconomics
Because they can probably get approved as Macro III and Micro III. 

Behavioral Finance was very interesting as well but a though course with assignments every week.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. You do travel a lot by train, maybe more than I expected, and therefore do use some money on train tickets.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I had heard that public transport was very expensive but was surprised to learn that it was cheaper than expected because i could get student discount. 
Eating out was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a free gym located at many different locations around Zurich. Very nice! They offer so many different classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sign up for ASVZ (the gym) and try out different classes. 
Also sign up for events with ESN Zurich. They do a lot of nice events for exchange students and you get to meet a lot of nice people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the rest of Switzerland on the weekends! If you are traveling in a group of 4 below 25 you can travel all over Switzerland for one day for inly 20CHF. Very cheap

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I would say. Switzerland reminded me a bit of DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to ESN events or just other event in general.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Swiss where a bit closed and reserved. I mostly spoke with other exchange students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The mountains and the active lifestyle the Swiss have. They also enjoy hiking and usually spend their weekends in the mountains.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to welcome events and meet people. 
Explore the whole of Switzerland - so beautiful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont worry if you get an accommodation a bit far from the city center. Most students live a bit far away and commuting time up to 50 min is normal. Its difficult and expensive to find a place to live in the center.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from all over the world, getting new friends and having the experience of living in a different country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning when you dont know anyone it is hard and a bit scary to socialize. So to just put yourself out there and try to talk with strangers were a great challenge for me!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
